verses.text: 1:1Adam, Seth, Enosh,
1:2Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
1:3Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
1:4Noah. Noah’s sons: Shem, Ham, Japheth.
1:5Japheth’s sons: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Elishah, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
1:6Gomer’s sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
1:7Javan’s sons: Elishah, Tharsis, the Kitians, and the Rhodians.
1:8Ham’s sons: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
1:9Cush’s sons: Saba, Euilat, Sabatha, Regma, and Sebekatha. Regma’s sons: Saba and Oudadan.
1:10Cush begot Nimrod. He began to be a giant hunter on the earth.
1:17Shem’s sons: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad,
1:24Sala,
1:25Eber, Peleg, Ragau,
1:26Serug, Nahor, Terah,
1:27Abraham.
1:28Abraham’s sons: Isaac and Ishmael.
1:29These are the generations of Ishmael’s firstborn: Nabaioth, Kedar, Nabdeel, Mabsan,
1:30Masma, Idouma, Masse, Choddad, Thaiman,
1:31Jettour, Naphes, and Kedma. These are Ishmael’s sons.
1:32The sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bore him Zembran, Jexan, Madan, Midian, Sobak, and Soe. Jexan’s sons: Saba and Daidan.
1:33Midian’s sons: Gaipha, Opher, Enoch, Abida, and Eldaa. All these were Keturah’s sons.
1:34Abraham begot Isaac. Isaac’s sons: Esau and Jacob.
1:35Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, Ragouel, Jeoul, Jeglom, and Kore.
1:36Eliphaz’s sons: Teman, Omar, Sophar, Gootham, Kenaz, and, from Timna, Amalek.
1:37Ragouel’s sons: Nacheth, Zare, Some, and Moze.
1:38Seir’s sons: Lotan, Sobal, Sebegon, Ana, Deson, Osar, and Daison.
1:39Lotan’s sons: Chorri, Aiman, Ailath, and Namna.
1:40Sobal’s sons: Golam, Manachath, Gaibel, Sob, and Onam. Sebegon’s sons: Aia and Ana.
1:41Ana’s sons: Daison. Deson’s sons: Emeron, Eseban, Jethran, and Charran.
1:42Osar’s sons: Balaan, Zoukan, and Jokan. Daison’s sons: Os and Arran.
1:43These are their kings: Balak son of Beor, whose city was named Dennaba.
1:44Balak died, and Jobab son of Zara from Bosorra became king in his place.
1:45Jobab died, and Asom from the land of the Thaimans became king in his place.
1:46Asom died, and Adad son of Barad, who struck Midian in Moab’s plain, became king in his place. His city was named Geththaim.
1:47Adad died, and Samaa from Masekka became king in his place.
1:48Samaa died, and Saul from Rooboth beside the river became king in his place.
1:49Saul died, and Balaennon son of Achobor became king in his place.
1:50Balaennon son of Achobor died, and Adad son of Barad became king in his place. His city was named Phogor.
1:51Adad died. Edom’s chiefs were Chief Thamana, Chief Gola, Chief Jetheth,
1:52Chief Elibamas, Chief Elas, Chief Phinon,
1:53Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mabsar,
1:54Chief Megediel, Chief Heram. These were Edom’s chiefs.
2:1These are the names of Israel’s sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
2:2Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher.
2:3Judah’s sons: Er, Onan, Shelon, three. They were born to him by Shua’s daughter, the Canaanite woman. Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil before the Lord, and He killed him.
2:4Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Phares and Zara. Judah’s sons were five in all.
2:5Phares’s sons: Arson and Jemouel.
2:6Zara’s sons: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Chalchal, and Dara, five in all.
2:7Charmi’s sons: Achar, Israel’s obstructer, who broke faith concerning the devoted thing.
2:8Ethan’s sons: Azariah.
2:9Eseron’s sons who were born to him: Jirameel, Ram, Caleb, and Aram.
2:10Aram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Naasson, ruler of Judah’s house,
2:11Naasson begot Salmon, and Salmon begot Boaz,
2:12Boaz begot Obed, and Obed begot Jesse,
2:13and Jesse begot his firstborn Eliab; Amminadab was the second, Samaa the third,
2:14Nathanael the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
2:15Asom the sixth, David the seventh.
2:16Their sister: Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah’s sons were Abessa, Joab, and Asahel, three.
2:17Abigail bore Amessa. Amessa’s father was Jothor the Ishmaelite.
2:18Caleb son of Eseron begot Gazouba, a wife, and Jerioth. These were her sons: Joasar, Sobab, and Orna.
2:19Gazouba died, and Caleb took Ephrath for himself. She bore him Or,
2:20and Or begot Uri, and Uri begot Bezalel.
2:21After these things Eseron went in to the daughter of Machir, Galaad’s father. He took her when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
2:22Segub begot Jair. He had twenty-three cities in Galaad.
2:23Gedsour and Aram took Jair’s villages from them, Kanath and its villages, sixty cities. All these belonged to the sons of Machir, Galaad’s father.
2:24After Eseron died, Caleb came to Ephratha. Eseron’s wife Abia bore him Aschod, Thekoe’s father.
2:25The sons of Jeremeel, Eseron’s firstborn, were Ram the firstborn, Baana, Aran, and Asom his brother.
2:26Jeremeel had another wife, whose name was Atara. She was Ozom’s mother.
2:27The sons of Ram, Jeremeel’s firstborn, were Maas, Jamin, and Akor.
2:28Ozom’s sons were Samai and Jadae. Samai’s sons were Nadab and Abisour.
2:29Abisour’s wife was named Abichail. She bore him Achabar and Molid.
2:30Nadab’s sons: Salad and Apphaim. Salad died without children.
2:31Apphaim’s sons: Isemiel. Isemiel’s sons: Sosan. Sosan’s sons: Achlai.
2:32Jadae’s sons: Achisamai, Jether, Jonathan. Jether died without children.
2:33Jonathan’s sons: Phaleth and Ozaza. These were Jeremeel’s sons.
2:34Sosan had no sons, only daughters. Sosan had an Egyptian servant named Jochel,
2:35and Sosan gave his daughter to his servant Jochel as a wife, and she bore him Eththi.
2:36Eththi begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabed,
2:37and Zabed begot Aphalel, and Aphalel begot Obed,
2:38and Obed begot Jehu, and Jehu begot Azariah,
2:39and Azariah begot Chelles, and Chelles begot Eleasa,
2:40and Eleasa begot Sosomai, and Sosomai begot Salloum,
2:41and Salloum begot Jechemias, and Jechemias begot Elisama.
2:42The sons of Caleb, Jeremeel’s brother: Marisa his firstborn, who was Ziph’s father, and the sons of Marisa, Hebron’s father.
2:43Hebron’s sons: Kore, Thapous, Rekom, and Semaa.
2:44Semaa begot Raem, Jerkaan’s father, and Jerkaan begot Samai,
2:45and his son was Maon, and Maon was Baithsour’s father.
2:46Gaipha, Caleb’s concubine, bore Arran, Mosa, and Gezoue. Arran begot Gezoue.
2:47Jadai’s sons: Ragem, Jotham, Gersom, Phalet, Gaipha, and Sagaph.
2:48Caleb’s concubine Mocha bore Saber and Tharchna.
2:49She bore Sagaph, Marmena’s father, and Saou, Machabena’s father and Gaibaa’s father. Caleb’s daughter was Ascha.
2:50These were Caleb’s sons. The sons of Or, Ephratha’s firstborn: Sobal, Kariathiarim’s father,
2:51Solomon, Bethlehem’s father, and Arim, Baithgedor’s father.
2:52Sobal, Kariathiarim’s father, had sons: Araa, Esi, Ammanith,
2:53Emospheos, the city of Jair, Aithalim, Miphithim, Hesamathim, and Hemasaraim. From these came the Sarathaians and the Esthaolaians.
2:54Solomon’s sons: Bethlehem, Netophathi, Ataroth of Joab’s house, half the Manathi, Hesarei,
2:55the families of scribes dwelling at Jabes, Thargathiim, Samathiim, Sokathiim. These were the Kinaians who came from Mesema, father of Rechab’s house.
3:1These were David’s sons born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; the second, Daniel, by Abigail the Carmelite;
3:2the third, Absalom son of Mocha daughter of Tholmai king of Gedsour; the fourth, Adonijah son of Aggith;
3:3the fifth, Saphatias, by Abital; the sixth, Jethraam, by his wife Agla.
3:4Six were born to him in Hebron. He reigned there seven years and six months, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
3:5These were born to him in Jerusalem: Samaa, Sobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four by Bersabee daughter of Amiel,
3:6and Ibaar, Elisama, and Eliphalet,
3:7Nage, Naphag, and Janoue,
3:8Elisama, Eliada, and Eliphalet, nine.
3:9All these were David’s sons, except for the sons of the concubines; Themar was their sister.
3:10Solomon’s sons: Rehoboam; Abia his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
3:11Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
3:12Amasias his son, Azariah his son, Joathan his son,
3:13Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
3:14Amon his son, Josiah his son.
3:15Josiah’s sons: Joanan the firstborn, Joakim the second, Sedekias the third, Salloum the fourth.
3:16Joakim’s sons: Jechonias his son, Sedekias his son.
3:17The sons of Jechonia-asir: Salathiel his son,
3:18Melchiram, Phadaias, Sanesar, Jekemia, Osamo, and Denethi.
3:19Salathiel’s sons: Zerubbabel and Semei. Zerubbabel’s sons: Mosollamos and Ananias, and Salomith their sister,
3:20Asoube, Ool, Barachias, Asadias, and Asobaesd, five.
3:21Ananias’s sons: Phalletia, and Isaiah his son, Raphaia his son, Orna his son, Abdia his son, Sechenia his son.
3:22Sechenia’s son: Samaia. Samaia’s sons: Chattous, Joel, Mari, Noadia, and Saphat, six.
3:23Noadia’s sons: Elithenan, Hezekiah, and Ezrikam, three.
3:24Elithenan’s sons: Odouia, Eliasib, Phalaia, Akoun, Joanan, Dalaia, and Anani, seven.
4:1Judah’s sons: Phares, Arson, Charmi, Or, Soubal,
4:2and Raia his son. Soubal begot Jeth, and Jeth begot Achimi and Laad. These were the generations of the Sarathi.
4:3These were Aitam’s sons: Jezrael, Ragma, and Jabas. Their sister’s name was Eselebbōn.
4:4Phanouel was Gedor’s father, and Azer was Osan’s father. These were the sons of Or, Ephratha’s firstborn, Bethlehem’s father.
4:5Saour, Thekoe’s father, had two wives, Aoda and Thoada.
4:6Aoda bore him Ochazam, Hephad, Thaiman, and Astheran. All these were Aoda’s sons.
4:7Thoada’s sons: Sareth, Saar, and Ethnan.
4:8Kos begot Enob and Sabeba, and the generations of the brother of Rechab son of Jarim.
4:9Igabes was more renowned than his brethren. His mother called his name Igabes, saying, “I bore as gabes.” †

4:10Igabes called upon the God of Israel, saying, “If Thou dost indeed bless me and enlarge my borders, and Thy hand is with me, Thou wilt bring about knowledge, so that I am not humbled.” And God brought about all that he asked. †
4:11Caleb, Ascha’s father, begot Machir, who was Assathon’s father.
4:12Assathon begot Bathrephan, Phessee, and Thana, father of the city of Naas, brother of Eselon the Kenazite. These were the men of Repha.
4:13Kenaz’s sons: Othniel and Saraia. Othniel’s sons: Athath.
4:14Manathi begot Gophera. Saraia begot Joab, father of Ageaddair, for they were craftsmen.
4:15The sons of Caleb son of Jephonne: Hera, Ala, and Noom. Ala’s sons: Kenaz.
4:16His son: Geseel, Ameachi, Zapha, Zaira, and Eserael.
4:17Esri’s sons: Jether, Morad, Apher, and Jalon. Jether begot Maron, Semai, and Mareth, Esthemon’s father.
4:18His wife—she was Adia—bore Jared, Gedor’s father, Aber, Sochon’s father, and Jekthiel, Zano’s father. These were the sons of Gelia daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mored took.
4:19The sons of the woman Idouia, Nachem’s sister. Dalia was Keila’s father, and Semeion was Joman’s father. The sons of Naem, Keila’s father: Agarmi and Esthemoe Machathi.
4:20Semion’s sons: Amnon and Rana, Anan’s son, and Thilon. Isei’s sons: Zoath and Zoath’s sons.
4:21The sons of Selom son of Judah: Er, Lecha’s father, Laada, Maresa’s father, and the families of houses of ephrath abak belonging to Esoba’s house, †
4:22Joakim, the men of Chozeba, Joash, and Saraph, who dwelt in Moab; and he brought them back—abedirin athoukiin. †
4:23These were potters who dwelt in Nataim and Gadera. They grew strong with the king in his kingdom and dwelt there.
4:24Simeon’s sons: Namouel, Jamin, Jarib, Zare, and Saul,
4:25Salem his son, Mabasam his son, Masma his son,
4:26Amouel his son, Saboud his son, Zakchour his son, Semei his son.
4:27Semei had sixteen sons and three daughters, but their brethren did not have many sons. All their families did not multiply as much as Judah’s sons.
4:28They dwelt in Beersheba, Sama, Molada, and Esersoual,
4:29Balaa, Boasom, and Thoulad,
4:30Bathouel, Erma, and Seklag,
4:31Baithmarchaboth, half of Sosim, and the house of Baroumseorim. These were their cities until King David.
4:32Their farmsteads were Aitam, Enremmon, Thokkan, and Aisan, five cities,
4:33with all their farmsteads around these cities as far as Baal. This was their possession and their enrollment.
4:34Mosobab, Jemoloch, and Josia son of Amasia,
4:35Joel—and this one was Isabia’s son—son of Saraia, son of Asiel,
4:36Elioenai, Jakaba, Jasouia, Asaia, Ediel, Ishmael, and Banaia,
4:37Zouza son of Sephei son of Allon son of Jedia son of Samari son of Samaios.
4:38These passed through under the names of rulers in their generations, and in their ancestral houses they multiplied into a multitude.
4:39They went as far as the approach to Gerara, as far as the east of Gai, to seek pastures for their livestock.
4:40They found rich, good pastures. The land was broad before them, with peace and quiet, for those who formerly dwelt there were from Ham’s sons.

4:41These who are recorded by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. They struck their houses and the Minaioi found there, devoted them to destruction to this day, and settled in their place, because there were pastures for their livestock there.
4:42Some of them, from Simeon’s sons, went to Mount Seir, five hundred men, with Phalettia, Noadia, Raphaia, and Oziel, Jesi’s sons, as their rulers.
4:43They struck those who remained of Amalek and dwelt there to this day.

5:1The sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn—for he was the firstborn, but when he went up upon his father’s bed, he gave his blessing to his son Joseph, Israel’s son, and he was not entered in the genealogy for the firstborn rights.
5:2For Judah was mighty in strength among his brethren, and from him came a leader, but the blessing belonged to Joseph.
5:3The sons of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn: Enoch, Phallous, Arson, and Charmi.
5:4Joel’s sons: Semei and Banaia his son. The sons of Goug, Semei’s son:
5:5his son Micha, his son Recha, his son Baal,
5:6his son Beera, whom Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour deported. He was ruler of the Reubenites.
5:7His brethren by his ancestral family, in their enrollments according to their generations: the ruler Joel, Zacharia,
5:8and Balek son of Ozouz son of Sama son of Joel. He dwelt in Aroer, and toward Nabau and Beelmaon,
5:9and eastward he lived as far as the approaches of the wilderness from the River Euphrates, because their livestock were numerous in Galaad’s land.
5:10In Saul’s days they made war against the resident aliens, and they fell into their hands, dwelling in tents as far as all the east of Galaad.
5:11Gad’s sons lived opposite them in Basan as far as Selcha.
5:12Joel was the firstborn, Sapham the second, and Jani the scribe in Basan.
5:13Their brethren by their ancestral houses were Michael, Mosollam, Sebee, Joree, Jachan, Zoue, and Obed, seven.
5:14These were the sons of Abichail son of Uri son of Jidai son of Galaad son of Michael son of Isai son of Jouri son of Zaboucham,
5:15son of Abdiel son of Gouni, ruler of an ancestral house.
5:16They dwelt in Galaad, in Basan and their villages, and throughout Sharon’s surrounding region as far as its outlet.
5:17Their enrollment, all of them, was in the days of Joatham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

5:18The sons of Reuben and Gad and half Manasseh’s tribe had men of strength who carried shields and the sword, drew the bow, and were taught war: forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty who went out to the battle line.
5:19They made war against the Hagarenes, Ituraeans, Naphisaeans, and Nadabaeans,
5:20and they prevailed over them, and the Hagaraeans and all their tents were given into their hands. For they cried to God in the battle, and He listened to them because they hoped in Him.
5:21They captured their baggage: five thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys, and one hundred thousand human lives.
5:22Many fell wounded, for the war was from God. They settled in their place until the deportation.
5:23The half of Manasseh’s tribe dwelt in the land from Basan to Baalermon, Sanir, and Mount Aermon, and they multiplied in Lebanon.
5:24These were the chiefs of their ancestral houses: Opher, Isei, Eliel, Esdriel, Jermia, Odouia, and Jediel, men mighty in strength, renowned men, rulers of their ancestral houses.
5:25They broke faith with their fathers’ God and went whoring after the gods of the peoples of the land whom God had removed from before them.

5:26Israel’s God stirred up the spirit of Phaloch king of Assour and the spirit of Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour. He deported Reuben, the Gaddite, and half Manasseh’s tribe, and brought them to Chalach, Chabor, and the River Gozan, to this day.
5:27Levi’s sons: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari.
5:28Kaath’s sons: Ambram, Issaar, Hebron, and Oziel.
5:29Ambram’s sons: Aaron, Moses, and Mariam. Aaron’s sons: Nadab, Abioud, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
5:30Eleazar begot Phinees, and Phinees begot Abisou.
5:31Abisou begot Bokai, and Bokai begot Ozi.
5:32Ozi begot Zaraia, and Zaraia begot Mariel.
5:33Mariel begot Amariah, and Amariah begot Achitob.
5:34Achitob begot Sadok, and Sadok begot Achimaas.
5:35Achimaas begot Azariah, and Azariah begot Joanan.
5:36Joanas begot Azariah, who served as priest in the house Solomon built in Jerusalem.
5:37Azariah begot Amariah, and Amariah begot Achitob.
5:38Achitob begot Sadok, and Sadok begot Salom.
5:39Salom begot Chelkias, and Chelkias begot Azariah.
5:40Azariah begot Saraias, and Saraias begot Josadak.
5:41Josadak went in the deportation with Judah and Jerusalem by Nabouchodonosor’s hand.
6:1Levi’s sons: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari.
6:2These are the names of Gedson’s sons: Lobeni and Semei.
6:3Kaath’s sons: Ambram, Issaar, Hebron, and Oziel.
6:4Merari’s sons: Mooli and Omousi. These were Levi’s ancestral families according to their ancestral families:
6:5For Gedson: for Lobeni his son, Jeeth his son, Zemma his son,
6:6Joach his son, Addi his son, Zara his son, Jethri his son.
6:7Kaath’s sons: Amminadab his son, Kore his son, Asir his son,
6:8Elkanah his son, Abiasaph his son, Asir his son,
6:9Thaath his son, Uriel his son, Ozia his son, Saul his son.
6:10Elkanah’s sons: Amasi and Achimoth,
6:11Elkanah his son, Souphi his son, and Naath his son,
6:12Eliab his son, Jidaer his son, Elkanah his son.
6:13Samuel’s sons: the firstborn, Sani, and Abia.
6:14Merari’s sons: Mooli; Lobeni his son, Semei his son, Oza his son,
6:15Somea his son, Aggia his son, Asaia his son.
6:16These are those David appointed over the work of the singers in the Lord’s house when the ark came to rest,

6:17and they ministered with instruments before the tent of the house of testimony until Solomon built the Lord’s house in Jerusalem. They took their places for their ministries according to their prescribed order.
6:18These are those who took their places, with their sons, from Kaath’s sons: Heman the psalm singer, son of Joel son of Samuel,
6:19son of Elkanah son of Edad son of Eliel son of Thie,
6:20son of Souph son of Elkanah son of Meth son of Amasias,
6:21son of Elkanah son of Joel son of Azariah son of Saphania,
6:22son of Thaath son of Asir son of Abiasaph son of Kore,
6:23son of Issaar son of Kaath son of Levi son of Israel.
6:24His brother Asaph stood at his right: Asaph son of Barachia son of Samaa,
6:25son of Michael son of Maasia son of Melchia,
6:26son of Athani son of Zarai son of Adia,
6:27son of Ethan son of Zamma son of Semei,
6:28son of Hecha son of Gedson son of Levi.
6:29The sons of Merari their brother were on the left: Ethan son of Kisai son of Abdi son of Maloch,
6:30son of Asebi son of Amessia son of Chelkios,
6:31son of Amasai son of Bani son of Semmer,
6:32son of Mooli son of Mousi son of Merari son of Levi.
6:33Their brethren, according to their ancestral houses, the Levites, were assigned to all the work of ministry of the tent of God’s house.

6:34Aaron and his sons burned incense on the altar of whole burnt offerings and on the incense altar, for all the work of the Holy of Holies and to make atonement for Israel, according to everything Moses, God’s servant, commanded.
6:35These were Aaron’s sons: Eleazar his son, Phinees his son, Abisou his son,
6:36Bokai his son, Ozi his son, Zaraia his son,
6:37Mariel his son, Amariah his son, Achitob his son,
6:38Sadok his son, Achimaas his son.
6:39These were their dwelling places in their villages within their boundaries, for Aaron’s sons of the Kaathi ancestral family, for the lot fell to them.
6:40They gave them Hebron in Judah’s land and its surrounding lands all around it.
6:41They gave the city’s plains and its villages to Caleb son of Jephonne.
6:42To Aaron’s sons they gave the cities of refuge: Hebron, Lobna and its surrounding lands, Selna and its surrounding lands, and Esthamo and its surrounding lands,
6:43Jeththar and its surrounding lands, Dabir and its surrounding lands,
6:44Asan and its surrounding lands, Attan and its surrounding lands, Basamys and its surrounding lands,

6:45and from Benjamin’s tribe, Gabee and its surrounding lands, Galemeth and its surrounding lands, Anchoch and its surrounding lands. All their cities were thirteen cities according to their ancestral families.
6:46For Kaath’s remaining sons, from the ancestral families, from the tribe, from half Manasseh’s tribe, there were ten cities by lot.
6:47For Gedson’s sons according to their ancestral families, from Issachar’s tribe, Asher’s tribe, Naphtali’s tribe, and Manasseh’s tribe in Basan, there were thirteen cities.
6:48For Merari’s sons according to their ancestral families, from Reuben’s tribe, Gad’s tribe, and Zebulun’s tribe, there were twelve cities by lot.
6:49Israel’s sons gave the Levites the cities and their surrounding lands,
6:50and they gave by lot, from the tribe of Judah’s sons and the tribe of Simeon’s sons, these cities which he called by name.
6:51Some of the ancestral families of Kaath’s sons had the cities of their boundaries from Ephraim’s tribe.
6:52They gave him the cities of refuge: Sychem and its surrounding lands in Mount Ephraim, and Gazer and its surrounding lands,
6:53Jekmaam and its surrounding lands, Baithoron and its surrounding lands,
6:54Eglam and its surrounding lands, Gethremmon and its surrounding lands,
6:55and from half Manasseh’s tribe, Anar and its surrounding lands, Jeblaam and its surrounding lands, according to the ancestral family of Kaath’s remaining sons.
6:56For Gedson’s sons, from the ancestral families of half Manasseh’s tribe: Golan in Basan and its surrounding lands, Aseroth and its surrounding lands,

14:5Ibaar, Elisae, and Eliphalet,
14:6Nage, Naphag, and Janouou,
14:7Elisamae, Balegdae, and Eliphalet.
14:8The foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David. David heard and went out to meet them.
14:9The foreigners came and fell upon the Valley of the Giants.
14:10David inquired through God, saying, “Shall I go up against the foreigners, and wilt Thou give them into my hands?” The Lord said to him, “Go up, and I will give them into your hands.”
14:11He went up to Baalpharasin, and David struck them there. David said, “God has cut through my enemies by my hand like a cutting of water.” Therefore he called that place the Cutting of Pharasin.
14:12They abandoned their gods there, and David ordered that they be burned with fire.
14:13The foreigners came again and again fell upon the Valley of the Giants.
14:14David again inquired of God, and God said to him, “Do not go behind them. Turn away from them and approach them near the pear trees.
14:15When you hear the sound of shaking in the tops of the pear trees, then go out to war, for God has gone out before you to strike the foreigners’ camp.”
14:16He did as God commanded him, and he struck the foreigners’ camp from Gabaon to Gazara.
14:17David had a name throughout all the land, and the Lord placed the fear of him upon all the nations.
15:1He made houses for himself in the City of David, prepared the place for God’s ark, and made a tent for it.
15:2Then David said, “No one may lift God’s ark except the Levites, for the Lord chose them to lift the Lord’s ark and to minister to Him for ever.”
15:3David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the Lord’s ark up to the place he had prepared for it.
15:4David gathered Aaron’s sons and the Levites.
15:5From Kaath’s sons: Ouriel the ruler and his brethren, one hundred twenty.
15:6From Merari’s sons: Asaia the ruler and his brethren, two hundred fifty.
15:7From Gersam’s sons: Joel the ruler and his brethren, one hundred fifty.
15:8From Elisaphan’s sons: Samaias the ruler and his brethren, two hundred.
15:9From Hebron’s sons: Eliel the ruler and his brethren, eighty.
15:10From Oziel’s sons: Amminadab the ruler and his brethren, one hundred twelve.
15:11David summoned Sadok and Abiathar the priests, and the Levites Ouriel, Asaia, Joel, Samaia, Eliel, and Amminadab.
15:12He said to them, “You are rulers of the Levites’ ancestral houses. Purify yourselves, you and your brethren, and bring up the ark of Israel’s God to the place I have prepared for it.
15:13Because you were not there previously, our God cut among us, for we did not seek according to judgment.”
15:14The priests and Levites purified themselves to bring up the ark of Israel’s God.
15:15The Levites’ sons took God’s ark, as Moses had commanded by God’s word according to the writing, with carrying poles upon them.
15:16David said to the Levites’ rulers, “Appoint their brethren the psalm singers with song instruments—harps, lyres, and cymbals—to sound on high with a voice of gladness.”
15:17The Levites appointed Aiman son of Joel; from his brethren, Asaph son of Barachia; and from Merari’s sons, his brethren, Aithan son of Kisaiou.
15:18With them were their brethren of the second rank: Zacharias, Oziel, Semiramoth, Jiiel, Oni, Eliab, Banaia, Maasaia, Mattathia, Eliphalia, Makenia, Abdedom, Jiiel, and Ozias, the gatekeepers.
15:19The psalm singers Aiman, Asaph, and Aithan were to make themselves heard with bronze cymbals.
15:20Zacharias, Oziel, Semiramoth, Jiiel, Oni, Eliab, Masaias, and Banaias played harps according to Alaimoth. †
15:21Mattathias, Eliphalias, Makenias, Abdedom, Jiiel, and Ozias played lyres, Amasenith, to strengthen. †
15:22Chonenia, ruler of the Levites, was ruler of the songs, for he was discerning.
15:23Barachia and Elkana were gatekeepers of the ark.
15:24The priests Sobnia, Josaphat, Nathanael, Amasai, Zacharia, Banai, and Eliezer sounded trumpets before God’s ark; Abdedom and Jia were gatekeepers of God’s ark.
15:25David, Israel’s elders, and the commanders of thousands went to bring up the ark of the Lord’s covenant from Abdedom’s house with gladness.
15:26When God strengthened the Levites lifting the ark of the Lord’s covenant, they sacrificed seven calves and seven rams.

15:27David was girded in a fine-linen robe, as were all the Levites lifting the ark of the Lord’s covenant, the psalm singers, and Chonenias, leader of the singers’ songs. Upon David was a fine-linen robe.
15:28All Israel brought up the ark of the Lord’s covenant with signals, the sound of the sopher, trumpets, and cymbals, sounding out with harps and lyres. †
15:29As the ark of the Lord’s covenant came to the City of David, Melchol daughter of Saul peered through the window. She saw King David dancing and playing, and despised him in her soul.
16:1They brought God’s ark and set it firmly in the middle of the tent David had pitched for it; they presented whole burnt offerings and offerings of deliverance before God.
16:2David finished presenting whole burnt offerings and offerings of deliverance, and blessed the people in the Lord’s name.
16:3He distributed to every Israelite, man and woman alike, to each, one baker’s loaf and a cake.
16:4He appointed some Levites to minister before the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to sound out, give thanks, and praise the Lord, Israel’s God:
16:5Asaph the leader, Zacharias second to him, Jiiel, Semiramoth, Jiiel, Mattathias, Eliab, Banaias, Abdedom, and Jiiel, with instruments, harps, and lyres; Asaph sounded the cymbals.
16:6Banaias and Oziel the priests sounded trumpets continually before the ark of God’s covenant.
16:7On that day David first appointed praise of the Lord through Asaph and his brethren:
16:8Give thanks unto the Lord; call upon Him by His name; make His works known among peoples. †
16:9Sing unto Him and hymn Him; recount to everyone His wonders, which the Lord has done.
16:10Praise in His holy name; the heart seeking His good pleasure shall rejoice.
16:11Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek His face continually.
16:12Remember His wonders which He has done, portents and judgments of His mouth,
16:13you offspring of Israel, His servants, sons of Jacob His chosen ones.
16:14He is the Lord our God; His judgments are throughout all the earth.
16:15He remembers His covenant for ever, His word which He commanded for a thousand generations,
16:16which He established with Abraham, and His oath to Isaac.
16:17He established it for Jacob as an ordinance, for Israel as an everlasting covenant,
16:18saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan, the measured allotment of your inheritance,” †
16:19when they became few in number, as they were made small and dwelt as strangers in it.
16:20They traveled from nation to nation, from a kingdom to another people.
16:21He allowed no man to overpower them and reproved kings on their account:
16:22“Do not touch My anointed ones, and do not act wickedly against My prophets.”
16:23Sing unto the Lord, all the earth; proclaim His salvation from day to day.
16:25For the Lord is great and greatly to be praised; He is fearsome above all the gods.
16:26For all the nations’ gods are idols, but our God made heaven.
16:27Glory and praise are before Him; strength and boasting are in His place.
16:28Give unto the Lord, ancestral families of the nations; give to the Lord glory and strength.
16:29Give unto the Lord the glory of His name; take gifts and bring them before Him, and bow before the Lord in His holy courts. †
16:30Let all the earth fear before Him; let the earth be set right and not be shaken.
16:31Let heaven be glad and the earth exult; let them say among the nations, “The Lord reigns!”
16:32The sea shall resound with its fullness, and the tree of the field and everything in it.
16:33Then the trees of the forest shall be glad before the Lord, for He has come to judge the earth.
16:34Give thanks unto the Lord, for it is good, for His mercy endures for ever. †
16:35Say, “Save us, O God of our salvation, and rescue us from the nations, that we may praise Thy holy name and glory in Thy praises.”
16:36Blessed be the Lord, Israel’s God, from age to age! All the people shall say, “Amen.” And they praised the Lord.
16:37They left Asaph and his brethren there before the ark of the Lord’s covenant to minister continually before the ark, each day’s duty on its day,
16:38with Abdedom and his brethren, sixty-eight; Abdedom son of Idithon and Ossa were gatekeepers.
16:39They left Sadok the priest and his brother priests before the Lord’s tent at Bama in Gabaon,

16:40to present whole burnt offerings to the Lord continually on the altar of whole burnt offerings, morning and evening, according to everything written in the Lord’s law, all He commanded Israel’s sons through Moses, God’s attendant;
16:41With him were Aiman, Idithon, and the remaining men chosen by name, to praise the Lord, for His mercy endures for ever.
16:42With them were trumpets and cymbals for sounding out, and instruments for God’s songs; Idithon’s sons were at the gate.
16:43All the people went, each to his house, and David returned to bless his household.
17:1When David was dwelling in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Behold, I dwell in a cedar house, but the ark of the Lord’s covenant is beneath skins.”
17:2Nathan said to David, “Do everything in your soul, for God is with you.”
17:3That night the Lord’s word came to Nathan, saying,
17:4“Go and say to David My servant, ‘Thus says the Lord: You shall not build Me a house for Me to dwell in it.
17:5For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day; I was in a tent and in a lodging.
17:6In all the places through which I passed in all Israel, did I ever speak unto one tribe of Israel appointed to shepherd My people, saying, “You have not built Me a cedar house”?
17:7Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold, from following the flocks, to become leader over My people Israel.
17:8I was with you wherever you went and destroyed all your enemies before you; I made you a name like the name of the great ones on the earth.
17:9I will appoint a place for My people Israel and plant them, and they shall dwell by themselves and no longer be anxious. Injustice shall no longer humble them as at the beginning.
17:10From the days when I appointed judges over My people Israel, I humbled all your enemies. I will increase you, and the Lord will build you a house.
17:11When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one who will be from your body, and prepare his kingdom.
17:12He shall build Me a house, and I will set his throne upright for ever.
17:13I will be a Father unto him, and he shall be a son unto Me. I will not withdraw My mercy from him, as I withdrew it from those before you. †
17:14I will make him secure in My house and in his kingdom for ever, and his throne shall be set upright for ever.’”
17:15Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and all this vision.
17:16King David went in and sat before the Lord. He said, “Who am I, O Lord God, and what is my house, that Thou hast loved me for ever?
17:17These things became small before Thee, God, and Thou didst speak of Thy servant’s house far ahead. Thou didst look upon me as a human vision, and Thou didst exalt me, Lord God.
17:18What more can David add unto Thee in giving glory? Thou knowest Thy servant.
17:19Thou hast done all this greatness according to Thy heart.
17:20Lord, there is none like Thee, and there is none besides Thee, according to all we have heard with our ears.

17:21There is no nation on the earth like Thy people Israel, whom God led to redeem a people for Himself, to make Himself a great and manifest name, driving nations out before Thy people whom Thou didst redeem from Egypt.
17:22Thou didst give Thy people Israel to Thyself as a people for ever, and Thou, O Lord, art their God.
17:23Now, Lord, let Thy word which Thou didst speak to Thy servant and concerning his house be made secure for ever,
17:24while people say, ‘Lord, Lord Almighty, God of Israel,’ and let the house of David Thy servant be set upright before Thee.
17:25For Thou, O Lord, didst open Thy servant’s ear to build him a house. Therefore Thy servant has found courage to pray before Thee.
17:26Now, Lord, Thou art God, and Thou hast spoken these good things concerning Thy servant.
17:27Now Thou hast begun to bless Thy servant’s house, so it may remain before Thee for ever. For Thou, O Lord, hast blessed it; bless it for ever.”
18:1After these things David struck the foreigners and routed them. He took Geth and its villages from the foreigners’ hand.
18:2He struck Moab, and Moab became servants to David, bringing gifts.
18:3David struck Adraazar king of Souba, Hemath, as he went to establish his hand upon the River Euphrates.
18:4David seized from them a thousand chariots, seven thousand horses, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David disabled all the chariots, but left a hundred chariots from them.
18:5The Syrian came from Damascus to help Adraazar king of Souba, and David struck twenty-two thousand men among the Syrian force.
18:6David placed a garrison in Syria near Damascus, and they became servants to David, bringing gifts. The Lord kept saving David in all his journeys.
18:7David took the golden collars that were upon Adraazar’s servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
18:8From Metabechas and from Adraazar’s choice cities David took a very great amount of bronze. From it Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.
18:9Thoa king of Hemath heard that David had struck the entire force of Adraazar king of Souba.

18:10He sent his son Idouram to King David to inquire after his peace and to bless him because he had fought Adraazar and struck him, for Thoa was a hostile man toward Adraazar. With him were all the silver and gold vessels.
18:11David consecrated these also to the Lord, with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: from Idumea, Moab, the sons of Ammon, the foreigners, and Amalek.
18:12Abessa son of Sarouia struck Idumea in the Valley of Salts: eighteen thousand.
18:13He placed garrisons in the valley, and all the Idumeans became David’s servants. The Lord kept saving David in all his journeys.
18:14David reigned over all Israel, and he administered judgment and righteousness for all his people.
18:15Joab son of Sarouia was over the army, and Josaphat son of Achiloud was recorder.
18:16Sadok son of Achitob and Achimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Sousa was secretary.
18:17Banaias son of Jodae was over the Chereththi and the Pheleththi, and David’s sons were the king’s foremost successors.
19:1After these things Naas king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son Anan reigned in his place.

19:2David said, “I will show mercy to Anan son of Naas, as his father showed mercy to me.” David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon to comfort him.

19:3The rulers of Ammon said to Anan, “Do you suppose David sent comforters to you to glorify your father before you? Have not his servants come to you so that they might search out the city and spy out the land?”
19:4Anan took David’s servants, shaved them, removed half their cloaks up to the fold, and sent them away.
19:5They came to report to David about the men. He sent to meet them because they had been greatly dishonored. The king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, then return.”

19:6The sons of Ammon saw that David’s people had been put to shame. Anan and the sons of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen for themselves from Syria of Mesopotamia, Syria of Moocha, and Soba.

19:7They hired thirty-two thousand chariots for themselves, and the king of Mocha and his people. They came and camped opposite Maidaba. The sons of Ammon gathered from their cities and came to wage war.
19:8David heard and sent Joab and the whole army of mighty men.
19:9The sons of Ammon came out and arrayed themselves for war beside the city gate. The kings who had come camped by themselves in the plain.
19:10Joab saw that opponents had come to fight him in front and behind. He selected from all the young men of Israel, and they arrayed themselves against the Syrian.
19:11He placed the remainder of the people in the hand of Abessa his brother, and they arrayed themselves opposite the sons of Ammon.
19:12He said, “If the Syrian prevails over me, you shall be my deliverance; and if the sons of Ammon prevail over you, I will save you.
19:13Act courageously, and let us strengthen ourselves for our people and for the cities of our God. The Lord will do what is good in His eyes.”
19:14Joab and the people with him arrayed themselves opposite the Syrians for war, and they fled from him.
19:15The sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, and they too fled before Joab and before Abessa his brother and entered the city. Joab came to Jerusalem.
19:16The Syrian saw that Israel had routed him. He sent messengers, and they brought out the Syrian from beyond the River, with Sophach, chief commander of Adraazar’s force, before them.
19:17David was informed. He gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came against them, and arrayed himself against them. The Syrian arrayed himself opposite David, and they fought him.
19:18The Syrian fled before David. David killed from the Syrian force seven thousand chariot fighters and forty thousand foot soldiers, and he killed Sophach the chief commander of the force.
19:19Adraazar’s servants saw that they had fallen before Israel. They made a covenant with David and served him, and the Syrian was no longer willing to help the sons of Ammon.

20:1In the following year, when the kings went out, Joab led the army’s entire force, and they devastated the country of the sons of Ammon. He came and besieged Rabba, while David remained in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabba and razed it.

20:2David took the crown of Molchol their king from his head. Its weight was found to be a talent of gold, with a precious stone in it, and it came upon David’s head. He brought out a very great amount of spoil from the city.
20:3He brought out the people who were in it and sawed them apart with saws and iron adzes. David did this to all the sons of Ammon. David and all his people returned to Jerusalem.
20:4After these things there was again war with the foreigners at Gazer. Then Sobochai the Ousathi struck Saphou, one of the sons of the giants, and humbled him.
20:5There was again war with the foreigners. Ellanan son of Jair struck Leemi, brother of Goliath the Geththite, whose spear shaft was like a weavers’ beam.
20:6There was again war at Geth. There was a man of extraordinary size whose digits were six and six, twenty-four; he too was descended from giants.
20:7He reproached Israel, and Jonathan son of Samaa, David’s brother, struck him.
20:8These belonged to Rapha in Geth. They were four giants in all, and they fell by David’s hand and by the hand of his servants.
21:1The devil stood in Israel and stirred David to number Israel. †
21:2King David said to Joab and the rulers of the force, “Go, number Israel from Bersabee to Dan, and bring the report to me, so that I may know their number.”

21:3Joab said, “May the Lord add to His people a hundredfold as many as they are, with my lord the king’s eyes seeing it! All are my lord’s servants. Why does my lord seek this? Let it not become sin for Israel!”
21:4The king’s word prevailed over Joab. Joab went out, passed through all Israel’s territory, and came to Jerusalem.
21:5Joab gave David the number of the people’s inspection: all Israel was a million and a hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Judah was four hundred eighty thousand men who drew the sword.
21:6He did not number Levi and Benjamin among them, because the king’s word had overpowered Joab.
21:7This matter appeared evil before God, and He struck Israel.
21:8David said to God, “I have sinned greatly in doing this thing. Now, I beseech Thee, take away Thy servant’s wickedness, for I have become exceedingly foolish.”
21:9The Lord spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying,
21:10“Go and speak to David, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am raising three things against you. Choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you.’”
21:11Gad came to David and said to him, “Thus says the Lord: Choose for yourself

21:12either three years of famine, or three months of your fleeing before your enemies and your enemies’ sword destroying, or three days of the Lord’s sword and death in the land, with the Lord’s angel destroying throughout Israel’s inheritance. Now consider what word I should answer Him who sent me.”
21:13David said to Gad, “All three press me very hard. I will indeed fall into the Lord’s hands, for His compassions are very many; but I will certainly not fall into human hands.”
21:14The Lord sent death upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

21:15God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. As he destroyed, the Lord saw and relented concerning the calamity. He said to the destroying angel, “Let it be enough for you! Relax your hand.” The Lord’s angel was standing at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.

21:16David lifted his eyes and saw the Lord’s angel standing between earth and heaven, with his drawn sword in his hand, stretched over Jerusalem. David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

21:17David said to God, “Was it not I who ordered the people to be numbered? I am the one who sinned; in doing evil I did evil. But these sheep—what have they done? Lord God, let Thy hand be upon me and my father’s house, and not upon Thy people for destruction, Lord.”
21:18The Lord’s angel told Gad to tell David to go up and establish an altar to the Lord at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
21:19David went up according to Gad’s word, which he had spoken in the Lord’s name.
21:20Orna turned and saw the king, and his four sons with him were methachabin. Orna was threshing wheat. †
21:21David came to Ornan. Orna came out from the threshing floor and bowed to David with his face to the ground.
21:22David said to Orna, “Give me your threshing-floor site, and I will build an altar to the Lord on it. Give it to me for its worth in silver, and the plague will cease from the people.”

21:23Orna said to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good before him. Behold, I give the calves for a whole burnt offering, the plow and the wagons for wood, and the grain for a sacrifice. I give everything.”
21:24King David said to Orna, “No! I will surely buy it for its worth in silver. I will not take what is yours for the Lord, to offer a whole burnt offering unto the Lord for nothing.”
21:25David gave Orna at his site six hundred shekels of gold by weight.

21:26David built an altar there to the Lord and offered whole burnt offerings and a deliverance offering. He cried to the Lord, and He answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of whole burnt offering, and consumed the whole burnt offering.
21:27The Lord spoke to the angel, and he put the sword into its sheath.
21:28At that time, when David saw that the Lord had answered him at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
21:29The Lord’s tent, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of whole burnt offerings were at that time in Bama at Gabaon.
21:30David could not go before it to seek God, because he hastened away from the sword of the Lord’s angel.
22:1David said, “This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar for whole burnt offering for Israel.”
22:2David ordered all the resident foreigners in Israel’s land to be gathered. He appointed quarrymen to cut dressed stones for building a house for God.
22:3David prepared much iron for the nails of the doorways and gates and for hinges, and bronze in abundance, beyond weighing.
22:4There were cedar timbers beyond counting, because the Sidonians and Tyrians brought cedar timbers to David in abundance.

22:5David said, “My son Solomon is a tender child, and the house to be built for the Lord must rise to greatness, renowned and glorious throughout all the earth. I will prepare for it.” David prepared in abundance before his death.
22:6He called Solomon his son and commanded him to build the house for the Lord, the God of Israel.
22:7David said to Solomon, “Child, it came upon my soul to build a house for the name of the Lord God.

22:8But the Lord’s word came upon me, saying, ‘You have poured out much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for My name, because you have poured out much blood upon the earth before Me.

22:9Behold, a son is born unto you; he shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all the enemies round about him, for Solomon is his name; and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days. †
22:10He will build a house for My name. He will be a son to Me, and I will be a Father to him. I will set upright the throne of his kingdom in Israel for ever.’
22:11Now, my son, the Lord will be with you, and He will grant success, and you will build a house for the Lord your God, as He spoke concerning you.
22:12Only may the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, and strengthen you over Israel, to observe and to do the law of the Lord your God.
22:13Then He will grant success, if you take care to do the ordinances and judgments that the Lord commanded Moses concerning Israel. Act courageously and be strong; do not fear or be terrified.

22:14Behold, according to my poverty I have prepared for the Lord’s house a hundred thousand talents of gold and a million talents of silver, with bronze and iron beyond weighing because there is so much. I have also prepared timber and stones; add to these.
22:15With you are workers in abundance: artisans, builders in stone, carpenters in wood, and everyone skilled in every kind of work.
22:16In gold, in silver, in bronze, and in iron, there is no counting. Arise and act, and the Lord be with you.”
22:17David commanded all the rulers of Israel to support Solomon his son:
22:18“Is not the Lord with you? He has given you rest on every side, for He has given the land’s inhabitants into hands, and the land has been subjected before the Lord and before His people.

22:19Now give your hearts and your souls to seek the Lord your God. Arise and build a sanctuary for the Lord your God, to bring the ark of the Lord’s covenant and God’s holy vessels into the house being built for the Lord’s name.”
23:1David was old and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king in his place over Israel.
23:2He gathered all Israel’s rulers, the priests, and the Levites.
23:3The Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward. Their number, counting the men head by head, was thirty-eight thousand.
23:4Of these, twenty-four thousand were supervisors over the works of the Lord’s house, and six thousand were scribes and judges.
23:5Four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand praised the Lord with the instruments that he made for praising the Lord.
23:6David divided them into service courses according to Levi’s sons: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari;
23:7and according to Parosom, Edan, and Semei.
23:8Edan’s sons: Jiiel the ruler, Zethom, and Joel—three.
23:9Semei’s sons: Salomith, Jiiel, and Aidan—three. These were the ancestral rulers of Edan.
23:10The sons of Semei: Jeth, Ziza, Joas, and Beria. These were Semei’s sons—four.
23:11Jeth was the ruler, and Ziza the second. Joas and Beria did not have many sons, so they became one ancestral house for a single inspection.
23:12Kaath’s sons: Ambram, Issaar, Chebron, and Oziel—four.
23:13Ambram’s sons: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was distinguished to be consecrated as most holy, he and his sons for ever, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister, and to invoke His name for ever.
23:14As for Moses, the man of God, his sons were called into the tribe of Levi.
23:15Moses’ sons: Gersam and Eliezer.
23:16Gersam’s sons: Soubael the ruler.
23:17Eliezer’s sons were Raabia the ruler. Eliezer had no other sons, but Raabia’s sons increased greatly.
23:18Issaar’s sons: Salomoth the ruler.
23:19Chebron’s sons: Idoud the ruler, Amadia the second, Oziel the third, and Ikemias the fourth.
23:20Oziel’s sons: Michas the ruler and Isia the second.
23:21Merari’s sons: Mooli and Mousi. Mooli’s sons: Eleazar and Kis.
23:22Eleazar died and had no sons, only daughters. The sons of Kis, their kinsmen, took them as wives.
23:23Mousi’s sons: Mooli, Eder, and Jarimoth—three.

23:24These were Levi’s sons according to their ancestral houses, their ancestral rulers according to their inspection, by the number of their names, head by head, doing the works of ministry in the Lord’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
23:25For David said, “The Lord, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people and has dwelt in Jerusalem for ever.”
23:26The Levites were no longer carrying the tent and all its vessels for its ministry.
23:27For David’s last words record the number of Levi’s sons from twenty years old and upward,
23:28for he stationed them at Aaron’s hand to minister in the Lord’s house, over the courts and chambers, over the purification of all holy things, and over the works of ministry in God’s house:
23:29for the bread of presentation, the fine flour of the sacrifice, the unleavened flat cakes, the pan preparation, the mixed preparation, and every measure;
23:30and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks unto the Lord, and likewise in the evening;
23:31and over all the whole burnt offerings offered to the Lord on sabbaths, new moons, and feasts, by number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually for the Lord.
23:32They shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony and the charges of Aaron’s sons their brethren, to minister in the Lord’s house.
24:1The sons of Aaron had divisions. Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abioud, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
24:2Nadab and Abioud died before their father and had no sons. Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons, served as priests.
24:3David, Sadok from Eleazar’s sons, and Achimelech from Ithamar’s sons divided them according to their inspection, according to their ministry, according to their ancestral houses.

24:4Eleazar’s sons were found to have more rulers of the mighty men than Ithamar’s sons. He divided them: sixteen rulers of ancestral houses for Eleazar’s sons, and eight according to ancestral houses for Ithamar’s sons.
24:5He divided them by lots, these alongside those, because there were rulers of the holy things and rulers of the Lord among Eleazar’s sons and among Ithamar’s sons.

24:6Samaias son of Nathanael, the secretary from Levi, recorded them before the king and the rulers, with Sadok the priest, Achimelech son of Abiathar, and the ancestral rulers of the priests and Levites: one ancestral house at a time for Eleazar and one at a time for Ithamar.
24:7The first lot came out for Jarib, the second for Ideia,
24:8the third for Charem, the fourth for Seorim,
24:9the fifth for Melchia, the sixth for Miamin,
24:10the seventh for Kos, the eighth for Abia,
24:11the ninth for Jesus, the tenth for Sechenia,
24:12the eleventh for Eliasib, the twelfth for Jakim,
24:13the thirteenth for Ochchopha, the fourteenth for Isbaal,
24:14the fifteenth for Belga, the sixteenth for Emmer,
24:15the seventeenth for Chezir, the eighteenth for Aphesse,
24:16the nineteenth for Phetaia, the twentieth for Ezekiel,
24:17the twenty-first for Jachin, the twenty-second for Gamoul,
24:18the twenty-third for Dalaia, the twenty-fourth for Maasai.
24:19This was their inspection according to their ministry, to enter the Lord’s house according to their ordinance through Aaron their father, as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded.
24:20As for the remaining sons of Levi: of Ambram’s sons, Soubael; of Soubael’s sons, Jadia.
24:21For Raabia: Jesias the ruler.
24:22Of the Issari, Salomoth; of Salomoth’s sons, Jath.
24:23The sons of Jediou: Amadia the second, Jaziel the third, Jokom the fourth.
24:24Oziel’s sons: Micha; Micha’s sons: Samer.
24:25Micha’s brother: Isia; Isia’s sons: Zacharia.
24:26Merari’s sons: Mooli and Mousi; Ozia’s sons; Bonni’s sons.
24:27Merari’s sons belonging to Ozia, his sons: Isoam, Zakchour, and Abdi.
24:28Of Mooli: Eleazar and Ithamar. Eleazar died and had no sons.
24:29As for Kis: Kis’s sons, Iramael.
24:30Mousi’s sons: Mooli, Eder, and Jarimoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their ancestral houses.

24:31They too received lots as did their brethren, Aaron’s sons, before the king, Sadok, Achimelech, and the ancestral rulers of the priests and Levites: ancestral heads, araab, as his younger brethren. †

25:1King David and the rulers of the force appointed for the works the sons of Asaph, Aiman, and Idithon, who uttered inspired words with kinyrai, nablai, and cymbals. Their number was reckoned head by head, those working in their tasks: †
25:2Asaph’s sons: Zakchour, Joseph, Nathanias, and Erael, Asaph’s sons attached to Asaph the prophet, attached to the king.
25:3Of Idithon: Idithon’s sons, Godolia, Souri, Isaia, Semei, Asabia, and Mattathias—six—with their father Idithon, striking the kinyra in thanksgiving and praise to the Lord.
25:4Of Aiman: Aiman’s sons, Boukias, Manthanias, Azarael, Soubael, Jerimoth, Ananias, Anani, Eliatha, Godollathi, Romemthi-od, Jesbakasa, Mallethi, Otheri, and Meazoth.
25:5All these were sons of Aiman, who played for the king in God’s words, to raise a horn. God gave Aiman fourteen sons and three daughters.
25:6All these were with their father, singing hymns in the Lord’s house with cymbals, nablai, and kinyrai, under the king and Asaph, Idithon, and Aiman.
25:7Their number, together with their brethren, was two hundred eighty-eight; they were taught to sing to the Lord, each with understanding.
25:8They too cast lots for the service courses, for the small and for the great, the accomplished and those learning.
25:9The first lot of his sons and his brethren came out for Asaph, for Joseph, Godolia; the second, Enia, his brethren and his sons—twelve.
25:10The third: Zakchour, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:11The fourth: Jesdri, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:12The fifth: Nathanias, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:13The sixth: Boukias, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:14The seventh: Iseriel, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:15The eighth: Josia, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:16The ninth: Manthanias, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:17The tenth: Semei, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:18The eleventh: Azaria, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:19The twelfth: Asabia, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:20The thirteenth: Soubael, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:21The fourteenth: Mattathias, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:22The fifteenth: Jerimoth, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:23The sixteenth: Ananias, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:24The seventeenth: Jesbakasa, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:25The eighteenth: Anani, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:26The nineteenth: Mellethi, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:27The twentieth: Eliatha, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:28The twenty-first: Ethir, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:29The twenty-second: Godollathi, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:30The twenty-third: Meazoth, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
25:31The twenty-fourth: Romemthi-od, his sons and his brethren—twelve.
26:1For the divisions of the gates: of the sons of Koreim, Mosollamia son of Kore, of Abiasaph’s sons.
26:2Mosollamia had sons: Zacharias the firstborn, Idiel the second, Zabadias the third, Jethnouel the fourth,
26:3Olam the fifth, Joanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh.
26:4Abdedom had sons: Samaias the firstborn, Jozabad the second, Joaa the third, Sochar the fourth, Nathanael the fifth,
26:5Amiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Phollathi the eighth, because God had blessed him.
26:6To Samaia his son were born sons of the firstborn Rosai for his ancestral house, because they were mighty.
26:7Samaia’s sons: Gothni, Raphael, Obed, Elzabad, and Achiou, mighty sons; Eliou, Sabchia, and Isbakom.
26:8All were from Abdedom’s sons, they and their brethren and their sons, working mightily in the labor: sixty-two in all belonging to Abdedom.
26:9Mosollamia had sons and brethren—eighteen mighty men.
26:10Osa, of Merari’s sons, had sons guarding the leadership, for he was not firstborn, and his father made him ruler
26:11of the second division; Tablai the third, Zacharias the fourth. All these, Osa’s sons and brethren, were thirteen.
26:12These divisions of gates, belonging to the rulers of the mighty men, had service courses like their brethren, to minister in the Lord’s house.
26:13They cast lots for the small and the great, according to their ancestral houses, for each gate.
26:14The eastern lot fell to Salamia and Zacharia. The sons of Joas cast lots for Melchia, and the lot came out northward.
26:15To Abdedom fell the south, opposite the house of esephin, †
26:16for the second; to Osa, westward beyond the gate of the chamber of the ascent, guard opposite guard.
26:17To the east, six each day; to the north, four each day; to the south, four each day; and for the esephin, two;
26:18for those relieving one another, and westward four, and for the path two relieving one another.
26:19These were the divisions of the gatekeepers belonging to Kore’s sons and Merari’s sons.
26:20The Levites, their brethren, were over the treasuries of the Lord’s house and the treasuries of the consecrated things.
26:21Ladan’s sons, the sons of the Gersoni belonging to Ladan, the ancestral rulers belonging to Ladan the Gersoni: Jiiel.
26:22Jiiel’s sons: Zethom and Joel, the brethren, over the treasuries of the Lord’s house.
26:23For Ambram, Issaar, Chebron, and Oziel:
26:24Soubael, the descendant of Gersam, the descendant of Moses, was leader over the treasuries.
26:25For his brother Eliezer were Raabias a son, and Josaias, Joram, Zechri, and Salomoth.

26:26This Salomoth and his brethren were over all the treasuries of the holy things that King David and the ancestral rulers, commanders of thousands and hundreds and leaders of the force, had consecrated,
26:27which he took from the wars and from the spoils, and from which he consecrated gifts so that the building of God’s house would not fall behind,

26:28and over all the holy things of Samuel the prophet, Saul the descendant of Kis, Abenner the descendant of Ner, and Joab the descendant of Sarouia: everything they consecrated was through the hand of Salomoth and his brethren.
26:29Of the Issari, Chonenia and his sons were assigned the outside labor over Israel, to act as scribes and give judgments.
26:30Of the Chebroni, Asabias and his brethren, mighty men, a thousand seven hundred, had oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan toward the west for all the Lord’s ministry and the king’s work.

26:31Of the Chebroni, Joudias was ruler of the Chebroni according to their generations and ancestral houses. In the fortieth year of his reign they were inspected, and a mighty man was found among them at Jazer in Galaaditis,

26:32and his brethren, mighty men, were two thousand seven hundred ancestral rulers. King David appointed them over the Roubeni, the Gaddi, and half the tribe of Manasseh for every ordinance of the Lord and word of the king.

27:1The sons of Israel according to their number, the ancestral rulers, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and scribes ministered to the people and attended to every word of the king according to divisions, in every matter of coming in and going out month by month throughout all the months of the year. Each division had twenty-four thousand.
27:2Over the first division, for the first month, was Jesboam son of Zabdiel. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:3He was of Phares’s sons, ruler of all the commanders of the force for the first month.
27:4Over the division of the second month was Dodia the Echochi. His division had twenty-four thousand, commanders of the force.
27:5The third, for the third month, was Banaias son of Jodae, the priest, the ruler. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:6This Banaias was mightier than the thirty and over the thirty. His son Amizabath was over his division.
27:7The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asael, Joab’s brother, and his son Zabdias and the brethren. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:8The fifth, for the fifth month, was the leader Samaoth the Jesrae. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:9The sixth, for the sixth month, was Odouias son of Ekkes the Thekoite. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:10The seventh, for the seventh month, was Chelles from Phallous, of Ephraim’s sons. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:11The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sobochai the Isathi, belonging to the Zarai. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:12The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer from Anathoth, from Benjamin’s land. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:13The tenth, for the tenth month, was Meera from Netouphat, belonging to the Zarai. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:14The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Banaias from Pharathon, of Ephraim’s sons. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:15The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Choldai the Netophati, belonging to Gothoniel. His division had twenty-four thousand.
27:16Over Israel’s tribes: for Reuben, Eliezer son of Zechri was leader; for Simeon, Saphatias son of Maacha;
27:17for Levi, Asabias son of Kamouel; for Aaron, Sadok;
27:18for Judah, Eliab, one of David’s brethren; for Issachar, Ambri son of Michael;
27:19for Zaboulon, Samaias son of Abdiou; for Nephthali, Jerimoth son of Esriel;
27:20for Ephraim, Ose son of Oziou; for half the tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Phadaia;
27:21for half the tribe of Manasseh in Galaad, Jaddai son of Zabdiou; for Benjamin’s sons, Asiel son of Abenner;
27:22For Dan, Azarael son of Joram. These were the ancestral heads of Israel’s tribes.
27:23David did not take their number from twenty years old and downward, because the Lord had said He would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
27:24Joab son of Sarouia began numbering among the people but did not finish. In these matters wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not registered in the book of King David’s daily records.
27:25Over the king’s treasuries was Asmoth son of Odiel. Over the storehouses in the countryside, villages, settlements, and towers was Jonathan son of Oziou.
27:26Over the workers farming the land was Esdri son of Choloub.
27:27Over the estates was Semei from Rama. Over the wine stores in the estates was Zachri son of Sephni.
27:28Over the olive groves and sycamores in the plain was Balanas the Gedorite. Over the oil stores was Joas.
27:29Over the grazing cattle in Asidon was Satrais the Sharonite. Over the cattle in the valleys was Sophat son of Adli.
27:30Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite. Over the donkeys was Jadias from Merathon.
27:31Over the sheep was Jaziz the Agarite. All these were overseers of King David’s possessions.
27:32Jonathan, David’s paternal uncle, was a counselor, an understanding man and a scribe. Jiiel son of Achamani was with the king’s sons.
27:33Achitophel was the king’s counselor, and Chousi was the king’s first friend.
27:34After this man, Achitophel; next was Jodae son of Banaiou and Abiathar, and Joab was the king’s chief commander.

28:1David assembled in Jerusalem all Israel’s rulers: the rulers of the judges, the rulers of the service courses attending the king’s person, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the treasury keepers, those over his possessions, the powerful men, and the army’s warriors.

28:2David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, “Hear me, brethren and my people. It came upon my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the Lord’s covenant and a standing place for our Lord’s feet, and I prepared the things suitable for the dwelling.
28:3But God said, ‘You shall not build Me a house to have My name called upon it, because you are a warrior and have shed blood.’

28:4The Lord, the God of Israel, chose me from all my father’s house to be king over Israel for ever. He chose the royal power in Judah, and from Judah’s house my father’s house, and among my father’s sons He was willing that I become king over all Israel.
28:5From all my sons—for the Lord gave me many sons—He chose Solomon my son to seat him upon the throne of the Lord’s kingdom over Israel.
28:6God said to me, ‘Solomon your son will build My house and My court, for I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be a Father to him,
28:7and I will set his kingdom upright for ever, if he remains strong to observe My commandments and My judgments, as on this day.’

28:8Now, before the whole assembly of the Lord and in the ears of our God, observe and seek all the commandments of the Lord our God, so that you may inherit the good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your sons after you for ever.

28:9And now, Solomon my son, know the God of your fathers, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul; for the Lord examines every heart and knows every thought. If you seek Him, He shall be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you utterly. †
28:10See, therefore, that the Lord has chosen you to build Him a house as a sanctuary. Be strong and act.”
28:11David gave Solomon his son the pattern of the temple, its houses, its zakcho, its upper rooms, its inner storerooms, and the house of propitiation; †
28:12and the pattern he had in his spirit: the courts of the Lord’s house, all the surrounding chambers for the storerooms of the Lord’s house, and the storerooms of the holy things;
28:13and the lodgings of the priests’ and Levites’ service courses for all the work of ministry in the Lord’s house, and the storerooms of the service vessels for worship in the Lord’s house.
28:14He gave the measure of their weight, both the gold and the silver ones;
28:15he gave him the weight of the lampstands and of the lamps.
28:16Likewise he gave him the weight of the tables of presentation, each golden table, and likewise of the silver ones;
28:17and of the meat hooks, libation vessels, and golden bowls, and the weight of the gold and silver ones, kephphoure of each weight. †
28:18He showed him the weight of the incense altar of tested gold, and the pattern of the chariot of the cherubim with outspread wings, overshadowing the ark of the Lord’s covenant.
28:19David gave Solomon everything in writing from the Lord’s hand, according to the understanding that had come to him about carrying out the pattern.

28:20David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong, be of good courage, and act. Do not fear or be dismayed, for the Lord my God is with you. He will not let you go nor forsake you, until you finish all the work of ministry in the Lord’s house.

28:21Behold, the service courses of the priests and Levites are ready for all ministry in God’s house, and are with you in every undertaking, together with everyone eager and wise in every craft. The rulers and all the people are ready for all your words.”
29:1King David said to the whole assembly, “Solomon my son, the one whom the Lord has chosen, is young and tender, and the work is great, for the building is for the Lord God, not for a human being.

29:2With all my strength I have prepared for my God’s house gold, silver, bronze, iron, timber, soom stones and filling stones, costly and variegated stones, every precious stone, and much Parian marble. †

29:3Moreover, because I delight in my God’s house, I have gold and silver that I have acquired for myself. Behold, I give it to my God’s house in addition, apart from what I have prepared for the house of holy things:
29:4three thousand talents of gold from Souphir and seven thousand talents of tested silver to coat the sanctuary’s walls with them,
29:5by the craftsmen’s hand. Who is eager to fill his hands today for the Lord?”
29:6The ancestral rulers, the rulers of Israel’s sons, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the overseers of the works, and the king’s stewards offered eagerly.

29:7They gave for the works of the Lord’s house five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand gold coins, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
29:8Those who had a stone gave it to the storerooms of the Lord’s house through Jiiel the Gersoni.
29:9The people rejoiced because of their eagerness, for they offered eagerly to the Lord with a full heart. King David rejoiced greatly.
29:10King David blessed the Lord before the assembly, saying, “Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting to everlasting.
29:11Thine, O Lord, are greatness, power, glory, victory, and strength; for Thou rulest all things in heaven and upon earth. Before Thee every king and nation is shaken. †
29:12From Thee come wealth and glory. Thou governest all, O Lord, Ruler of every rule. In Thy hand are strength and dominion; and it is in Thy hand, O Almighty, to make all things great and strong.
29:13Now, O Lord, we give thanks unto Thee, and praise the name of Thy glory.
29:14Who am I, and who are my people, that we had strength to offer willingly unto Thee in this manner? All things are Thine, and of Thine own have we given unto Thee.
29:15For we are resident strangers before Thee, and sojourners, as all our fathers were: our days upon earth are as a shadow, and there is no endurance. †
29:16Lord our God, all this abundance that I have prepared for a house to be built for Thy holy name is from Thy hand, and everything is Thine.

29:17I know, Lord, that Thou examinest hearts and lovest righteousness. In simplicity of heart I eagerly offered all these things. Now I have seen Thy people found here offer eagerly to Thee in gladness.
29:18Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel our fathers, preserve these things for ever in the thought of Thy people’s heart, and direct their hearts toward Thee.
29:19Give Solomon my son a good heart to do Thy commandments, testimonies, and ordinances, and to bring the construction of Thy house to completion.”

29:20David said to the whole assembly, “Bless the Lord your God.” The whole assembly blessed the Lord, the God of their fathers. Bending their knees, they prostrated themselves before the Lord and the king.

29:21On the day after the first day David sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord and offered whole burnt offerings to God: a thousand calves, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their libations, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
29:22They ate and drank before the Lord that day with joy. They made Solomon son of David king a second time and anointed him for the Lord as king, and Sadok for priesthood.
29:23Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father and was accepted with favor. All Israel obeyed him.
29:24The rulers, the powerful men, and all the sons of King David his father submitted to him.
29:25The Lord made Solomon exceedingly great before all Israel and gave him a king’s glory such as had not belonged to any king before him.
29:26David son of Jessai reigned over Israel
29:27for forty years: in Chebron seven years, and in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
29:28He died in a good old age, full of days, wealth, and glory. Solomon his son reigned in his place.
29:29The remaining deeds of King David, the earlier and the later, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet, and the records of Gad the seer,
29:30concerning all his kingdom and dominion, and the times that came upon him, upon Israel, and upon all the kingdoms of the earth.
